title: The centurion's faith (Luke 7:1–10)
hook: a Roman officer says: just say the word

segments.voice: Yesterday: a beam in the eye, a storehouse in the heart, and your line, out of the heart the mouth speaks.
screen: `OUT OF THE HEART THE MOUTH SPEAKS.`

segments.voice: A centurion was a military officer, and this one is not Jewish: an unlikely person at the center of a story about faith in a small Jewish town. In Capernaum, Luke says, his servant is dying, a servant "who was dear unto him." The first surprise: the centurion doesn't go to Jesus himself. He sends the elders of the Jewish community, and they plead his case warmly. He's worthy, they say: "For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue." A foreign officer, and the town's elders are his advocates.
screen: `THE ELDERS: HE BUILT US A SYNAGOGUE.`

segments.voice: So Jesus goes with them. When he's nearly at the house, the centurion sends friends with a message. In the King James words: "Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof." The elders said he's worthy. He says I'm not. A man who gives orders to soldiers, telling a traveling teacher, don't trouble yourself with me. Then he explains why Jesus needn't come at all: "say in a word, and my servant shall be healed. For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers, and I say unto one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh." He knows a word from the right person is enough, no matter the distance. Luke says Jesus "marvelled at him." This time Jesus is the one amazed. He turns to the crowd: "I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel." When the friends get back to the house, the servant is well. In Luke's version, the centurion and Jesus never meet face to face; the whole story happens through messengers, and a word sent across a distance. Catholics echo the centurion at Mass: just before communion, the people say they are not worthy for the Lord to come under their roof, but ask him only to say the word. An officer's message, still spoken in churches today.
screen: `A MAN UNDER AUTHORITY: SAY THE WORD.`
then, large: `SAY IN A WORD, AND MY SERVANT SHALL BE HEALED.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone you can't easily reach right now, a friend in another city, someone in a hospital bed or a hard season. Find a word short enough to fit in one breath, thinking of you, I'm here, and say it slowly in your mind, as if it were already on its way. If you pray, you can echo the centurion and ask God only to say the word for them; if you don't, simply hold the word and the person together.
Centurion. An officer who says he isn't worthy to have Jesus under his roof, and trusts that one word, sent from a distance, is enough.
Your line: only say the word. A word can travel where you can't. That's day five hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: At Catholic Mass, just before communion, the congregation says a form of the centurion's words, saying they are not worthy for the Lord to enter under their roof and asking him only to say the word.

fork.setup: you're a Roman officer. the teacher you asked for is almost at your door. what do you do?
options: meet him at the gate with honor.
send friends: don't trouble yourself; only say the word.
send soldiers to hurry him along.
fork.reveal: the centurion sends word that he isn't worthy to have Jesus under his roof, and that a word is enough. Jesus marvels at his faith.

original.note: Greek: commander of a hundred, a centurion.

trapdoor: what you thought: a soldier asks for a healing.
what it means: an outsider, vouched for by the town's elders, believes a word from Jesus can heal across a distance, and Jesus marvels.
what a scholar hears: in Luke the two never meet, while in Matthew the centurion comes himself; the whole story turns on a sent word.
guess: an army officer in charge of soldiers
a tax official collecting for Rome
a town elder who leads the synagogue

chat.says: Why didn't the centurion want Jesus to come all the way to his house?
options: He felt unworthy, and trusted that one word from Jesus was enough.
He was embarrassed by his house and didn't want anyone to see it.
He doubted Jesus could heal, so he sent the elders to call it off.
chat.meaning: He said he wasn't worthy to have Jesus under his roof, and that a word from the right person was enough, at any distance.

centurion.meaning: a military officer in charge of soldiers

Capernaum.meaning: the town where the centurion and his servant lived

synagogue.meaning: a Jewish house of prayer and study

communion.meaning: receiving the consecrated bread and wine at Mass

notes: The Mass response is described, not quoted (the current English wording is copyrighted).
'Still spoken in churches around the world' refers to the Mass response. Confirm.
'Marvelled' (thaumazo) applied to Jesus is rare in the Gospels (also Mark 6:6). Confirm 'almost never'.
Greek hekatontarches spelling in Luke 7:2 (Luke uses hekatontarches). Confirm.
